title: Mars: A Light That Answers
premise: A damaged landing strands a small expedition. Recovery becomes a rescue, then a return journey carrying people and evidence. This is an engineering story with recovered qualified systems, not real survival instructions.

stages.title: A voice above the ridge
stages.speaker: Mission Control
stages.motivation: We lost your signal on landing. Repair the radio and put a powered signal above the ridge. We are listening.

area.label: A voice above the ridge
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a voice above the ridge, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Place a powered radio or directed optical beacon on Contact ridge.

stages.title: Somewhere to come back to
stages.speaker: Mission Control
stages.motivation: The landing tore the habitat vestibule. The inner cabin still has its certified life-support unit. Make the entry weather-tight, store water, and protect a living tray. The missing survey crew may need this refuge too.

area.label: Somewhere to come back to
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to somewhere to come back to, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: Somewhere to come back to stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at somewhere to come back to. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: The route out
stages.speaker: Survey lead
stages.motivation: Our survey crawler is overdue. Your cargo sled holds the rover parts. Get moving and map the route before following its last transmission.

area.label: The route out
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to the route out, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Make the Rover drive under solar power.
Equip the rover with its seat harness.

caches.label: The route out stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at the route out. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: What the cliff can tell us
stages.speaker: Geologist
stages.motivation: The route crosses an exposed ice lens. Keep a sealed specimen and its photograph. A closer view of the layered cliff may tell us which route the crawler took, not what is safe without checking.

area.label: What the cliff can tell us
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to what the cliff can tell us, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: What the cliff can tell us stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at what the cliff can tell us. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: The sky is closing
stages.speaker: Weather officer
stages.motivation: Dust is obscuring the route. Restore the station so we can watch for a clear interval, and protect our spare controller before we move on.

area.label: Weather station apron
area.travelText: The mapped instrument apron is a short drive from the outcrop. We take the field kit and leave the sampling bench where it stands.

caches.label: Weather-station service cabinet
caches.narrative: The mothballed station was stored sensibly: its calibrated sensor mast, detached vane and complete logger are here together. A service enclosure and filter material can protect our spare controller.

stages.title: A voice in the static
stages.speaker: Orbital control
stages.motivation: The survey crew missed their last check-in. This relay can hear beyond the ridge. Bring it back on the air—we need to find out what happened.

area.label: Northern relay knoll
area.travelText: The weather record gives us a route to the relay knoll. We bring the map and leave the station measuring conditions behind us.

objectives.text: Bring the working relay onto the knoll and establish contact.

caches.label: Relay maintenance cabinet
caches.narrative: The relay itself is still here, with its complete antenna and charged powerpack stored beside it. Its service pouch holds a matched fuse; the fault indicator points to the old one.

stages.title: Not the only ones stranded
stages.speaker: Survey crew
stages.motivation: Our cabin is intact, but its drive has failed. The refuge is a short way along the route. Prepare it, then bring us there in the crawler—repair its drive or tow us. A hot meal would be welcome.

area.label: Survey recovery route
area.travelText: The message and map lead to the disabled crawler and the service refuge farther along the recovery route. We bring the rover and recovery kit; the working relay stays on its knoll.

objectives.text: Get the crew into shelter and give them a hot meal.

caches.label: Survey refuge and crawler stores
caches.narrative: The crew are waiting in their intact crawler cabin. Its service compartment holds a spare drive and towing equipment. The nearby field refuge, a short way along the recovery route, has bedding and food, but needs preparation before the crew can move in.

stages.title: A place to work, a voice home
stages.speaker: Survey crew
stages.motivation: We can do more than wait here now. Give us a lit place to work, and let our families hear our voices.

area.label: Recovery camp
area.travelText: We collect the known equipment needed for this work and move to recovery camp. Earlier work stays where we left it.

caches.label: Recovery camp stores
caches.narrative: The existing recovery camp has the following stored mission equipment; these are not a new delivery.

objectives.text: Send the crew’s recorded message home.

stages.title: The long night
stages.speaker: Camp engineer
stages.motivation: That service wall is losing heat overnight. Use the test chamber to understand it, then fit a screen so everyone can sleep comfortably.

area.label: Camp thermal workshop
area.travelText: We collect the known equipment needed for this work and move to camp thermal workshop. Earlier work stays where we left it.

caches.label: Camp thermal workshop stores
caches.narrative: The existing camp thermal workshop has the following stored mission equipment; these are not a new delivery.

objectives.text: Fit a thermal screen to the sleeping cabin.

stages.title: Enough water to stay
stages.speaker: Crew engineer
stages.motivation: The recovered crew know the ice-processing site. Its treatment skid is intact. Bring the water loop back into service so we can settle at camp and grow something again.

area.label: Enough water to stay
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to enough water to stay, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: Enough water to stay stores
caches.narrative: This is an existing ice-processing pilot site. Its enclosed melter, treatment skid, monitored tank and circulation pump were stored as working appliances. The disconnected return hose is still here.

stages.title: A meal that grew here
stages.speaker: Crew botanist
stages.motivation: We have time to wait for a crop, if we give it the right place to grow. The greenhouse shell survived at the camp. Bring it light, a clean growing bed and a dependable water supply.

area.label: A meal that grew here
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a meal that grew here, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Grow the potatoes and share a warm meal.

caches.label: A meal that grew here stores
caches.narrative: The camp greenhouse is mostly intact. Its growing tray, fan, light, brought substrate and seed potatoes were stored here for a later planting. A damaged seam needs the existing patch kit.

stages.title: Make what cannot be shipped
stages.speaker: Crew engineer
stages.motivation: The camp machine shop has stock and tools. Make a reliable replacement wheel and a protected sample carrier. They will let us take the next journey rather than patch this camp forever.

area.label: Make what cannot be shipped
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to make what cannot be shipped, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Equip the crawler with its mounted sample carrier.
Fit the replacement wheel module for the coming traverse.

caches.label: Make what cannot be shipped stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at make what cannot be shipped. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: Across the dark ground
stages.speaker: Survey lead
stages.motivation: The route to the old ascent depot crosses rough lava. We can reach it, but not by pretending our first map shows everything. Build a short-range scout and prepare the crawler for the surveyed ground.

area.label: Across the dark ground
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to across the dark ground, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Equip the crawler with its marked traverse.

caches.label: Across the dark ground stores
caches.narrative: The geology depot holds a stored Mars scout. Its delicate rotor assembly and battery were packed separately; its flight electronics, camera and legs are already fitted. A route tablet and hazard marker are also here.

stages.title: The route is not the ground
stages.speaker: Field engineer
stages.motivation: The scout found the channel, but it cannot tell us how the surface will carry the crawler. Check and mark the approach, then bring our wheel-equipped crawler to it.

area.label: Shallow channel
area.travelText: We collect the known equipment needed for this work and move to shallow channel. Earlier work stays where we left it.

caches.label: Shallow channel stores
caches.narrative: The existing shallow channel has the following stored mission equipment; these are not a new delivery.

objectives.text: Survey and mark the supported channel approach.
Bring the wheel-equipped crawler to the surveyed channel approach.

stages.title: What lies beneath
stages.speaker: Geologist
stages.motivation: The radar shows a buried boundary. Collect a core, examine its layers, and compare the measurements. Let the evidence decide what this place used to be.

area.label: What lies beneath
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to what lies beneath, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: What lies beneath stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at what lies beneath. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: The plant that breathes stone air
stages.speaker: Flight engineer
stages.motivation: The ascent depot was built to make oxygen here. Its reactor stack is intact, but the air intake and controls were dismantled for storage. Bring the recovered plant back into service.

area.label: The plant that breathes stone air
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to the plant that breathes stone air, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Restore the plant and service the ascent vehicle’s oxygen module.

caches.label: The plant that breathes stone air stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at the plant that breathes stone air. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: A ship with an unfinished job
stages.speaker: Flight engineer
stages.motivation: The pre-positioned ascent vehicle has waited longer than planned. Its sealed propulsion module survived. Restore the cabin and avionics using the depot parts, then let the built-in tests tell us what still fails.

area.label: A ship with an unfinished job
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a ship with an unfinished job, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: A ship with an unfinished job stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at a ship with an unfinished job. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: A moving meeting place
stages.speaker: Orbital navigator
stages.motivation: The orbiter is not above us all the time. We need a common clock and a measured beacon before we agree where to meet. Your old radio and patient observations matter again.

area.label: A moving meeting place
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a moving meeting place, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: A moving meeting place stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at a moving meeting place. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: What we take with us
stages.speaker: Survey crew
stages.motivation: We came here to explore, and we leave with more than a survival story. Pack the specimens with their records, leave the camp useful to the next crew, and bring everyone to the ship.

area.label: What we take with us
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to what we take with us, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

caches.label: What we take with us stores
caches.narrative: The expedition reaches the previously placed mission stores at what we take with us. These include the following recovered equipment, not freshly delivered ingredients.

stages.title: A light that answers
stages.speaker: Mission Control
stages.motivation: The recovered ascent vehicle is waiting. We have the cabin tests and agreed rendezvous. Complete the handover, then bring the people and their discoveries home.

area.label: A light that answers
area.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a light that answers, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Bring the ascent capsule to the orbiter hatch with the returned specimens.

sources.title: The Fact and Fiction of Martian Dust Storms
sources.note: Dust reduces sunlight and adheres to equipment; Mars winds are not Earth-hurricane force at the same speed.

sources.title: Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment
sources.note: A demonstrated engineered process, not an improvised household chemical combination.

sources.title: Where Should Future Astronauts Land on Mars? Follow the Water
sources.note: Near-surface ice is a candidate resource; accessibility varies.

sources.title: Ingenuity mission
sources.note: Thin atmosphere demands purpose-built flight hardware; recovered scout modules are fictional mission equipment.

sources.title: NASA thermal testing
sources.note: Controlled thermal testing of spacecraft and subsystems grounds the test-chamber setting; this fictional field comparison is not a qualification procedure.

sources.title: JPL rover navigation
sources.note: Terrain assessment and route selection matter for mobility. The field ground-probe interpretation remains a simplified fictional crewed-mission technique.

notes: Unreleased v5 whole-campaign candidate, not fresh-play validated. Incorporates the reviewed lighter v4 Weather/Relay/Rescue content.
Ready engineered equipment replaces preparation ladders. No steps were added solely to refill a count target.
Three new local episodes: camp cooperation/contact, controlled thermal investigation, and checking a scout route on the ground.
Current-scene packing only. Manufactured mission equipment and qualified processes are fictional abstractions, not survival or engineering instructions.
